text.title: HealthTech FHIR BA Pack Decision Tree

decision-tree.root-question: Does the feature read, write or transmit identifiable health data (PHI under HIPAA, special-category data under GDPR Art. 9, or NHS patient data)?

branch.conclusion: Skip this methodology. Without identifiable health data there is no FHIR mapping, BAA or consent obligation to pin; use the ordinary privacy BA pack.

branch.question: Is every clinical element mapped to a FHIR resource and profile, with coded fields bound to LOINC / SNOMED CT / RxNorm (or dm+d)?

branch.conclusion: Block. Produce the element-to-resource mapping table against the named profile before any data-flow or vendor work.
Block. Bind coded fields to the standard terminology with code-system URIs; keep free text only as `.text`.

branch.question: Do every PHI-touching processor, flow, consent and audit control meet the rules?

branch.conclusion: Block. Sign the BAA / Art. 28 agreement or strip PHI from the payload before data flows.
Block. Build the per-boundary flow table and de-identify analytics and model flows by a named method.

branch.when: research_use == true AND (irb_reference_missing == true OR consent_records_merged == true)
branch.conclusion: Block. Split treatment and research consent into versioned Consent records with the IRB protocol reference.
Block. Move the audit trail to append-only storage with six-year retention and per-patient query.
Block. Complete the minimum matrix rows and name the stricter clock per row.
Block. Encrypt the listed store, backup, index or log and separate key management before launch.
Produce the full pack: FHIR mapping, terminology bindings, flow table, processor list with agreements, overlap matrix, consent model, audit-trail spec, encryption inventory.

example.p: Feature ingests home blood-pressure readings, so phi_in_scope true. Readings mapped to Observation with LOINC codes. The error tracker captured request bodies with patient names and had no BAA → processor_without_agreement true → r-baa-or-dpa-per-processor: PHI scrubbed from error payloads and the BAA signed before launch.
